messages.content: The audit manager added a mandatory document review at the hotel Wednesday from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. Replace the Wednesday return with Thursday. I still need to join a San Francisco meeting at 1:00 p.m. Pacific.

I’ll keep the Sunday outbound and rework the return. For Thursday, January 16, the viable choices are a 6:10 a.m. nonstop from Raleigh-Durham arriving San Francisco at 9:18 a.m., or a 5:25 a.m. departure connecting in Denver and arriving at 10:42 a.m. A later 7:35 a.m. connection would not arrive until 12:38 p.m., which leaves essentially no margin before the meeting.
How much time does the nonstop leave after landing, and what is the fare difference?

The nonstop puts you in San Francisco 3 hours 42 minutes before the meeting. The Denver itinerary leaves 2 hours 18 minutes. The complete round trip is $684 with the nonstop return and $612 with the Denver return, so the nonstop costs $72 more.
What happens if the Denver flight is delayed? Is that connection comfortable?

The scheduled Denver connection is 54 minutes. It is valid, but a delay out of Raleigh could cause a missed connection, and the next available Denver-to-San Francisco flight would arrive after 1:00 p.m. The nonstop avoids that failure point and has the larger arrival buffer.
Then eliminate the connection. Confirm the outbound is still the Sunday flight that gets me to Raleigh around 7:15 p.m.

Yes. The outbound remains United 2186 on Sunday, January 12, departing SFO at 10:55 a.m. and arriving RDU nonstop at 7:14 p.m. The revised return is United 1769 on Thursday, January 16, departing RDU at 6:10 a.m. and arriving SFO nonstop at 9:18 a.m.
Check the practical timing from the hotel Thursday morning. I do not want to discover that the rental return makes 6:10 unrealistic.

The hotel is about 24 minutes from RDU at that hour. Leaving at 3:55 a.m. should put you at the rental return near 4:20 a.m.; allowing about 15 minutes for return and the shuttle gets you to the terminal around 4:35 a.m., 1 hour 35 minutes before departure. The rental facility is open and accepting returns then.
What fare and bag terms are attached to the $684 total?

It is regular economy in both directions, not basic economy. The ticket can be changed without a change fee, though any fare difference applies. It is nonrefundable to the original payment method. One carry-on and one personal item are included; a checked bag would cost $40 each way. Seats are available on both flights.
No checked bag. Give me the complete round trip once more before I authorize it.

Round trip for Priya Nair: Sunday, January 12, United 2186 nonstop SFO-RDU, 10:55 a.m.-7:14 p.m.; Thursday, January 16, United 1769 nonstop RDU-SFO, 6:10 a.m.-9:18 a.m. Regular economy, carry-on and personal item included, no checked bag, nonrefundable, changes permitted with fare difference. Total due is $684. The Thursday arrival is scheduled 3 hours 42 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. Pacific meeting.
That is correct. Purchase the complete round trip at $684.

Purchased for Priya Nair at $684: United 2186 nonstop from San Francisco to Raleigh-Durham on Sunday, January 12, departing 10:55 a.m. and arriving 7:14 p.m.; United 1769 nonstop from Raleigh-Durham to San Francisco on Thursday, January 16, departing 6:10 a.m. and arriving 9:18 a.m. Regular economy includes one carry-on and one personal item, with no checked bag added. The ticket is nonrefundable and changes may require a fare difference. The revised return accommodates the Wednesday 7:00-8:30 p.m. document review and is scheduled to arrive 3 hours 42 minutes before Thursday’s meeting.
